newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka army to give security for local poll.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka army to give security for local poll.

text.p: Sri Lanka's army will help provide security for forthcoming local government polls, already marred by widespread violence and the killing of a ruling coalition legislator, election officials said on Tuesday.

"The army will be used only for patrolling wherever there is trouble," Elections Commissioner Dayananda Dissanayake told Reuters. "They will supplement mobile police patrols and be under the direction of the police chief."

He said troops would be deployed in troubled areas and districts bordering the northern and eastern provinces, where Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils.
The local government elections, the first popularity test for President Chandrika Kumaratunga's People's Alliance (PA) coalition, are scheduled for March 21.
Other elections department officials said each of the 8,222 polling stations would be guarded by two policemen.
Dissanayake said soldiers would not be allowed near polling stations during the election.
The independent Island newspaper said on Tuesday that nearly 30,000 policemen would be deployed for the poll but gave no details.
The campaign has been hit by the killing of a governing coalition legislator last month, sparking two days of riots in the lawmaker's constituency of Ratnapura, 80 km (50 miles) southeast of Colombo.
An opposition United National Party (UNP) member of parliament and a former UNP mayor are among the suspects detained by police in connection with the killing.
The government has since launched a crackdown on illegal weapons used by politicians, granting an amnesty till March 15 for the surrender of illegal firearms.
Politicians and their supporters own large numbers of guns, many of them unlicensed, which they obtained in the late 1980s to protect themselves against left-wing insurgents and Tamil rebels.
An independent monitoring group said at the weekend a total of 944 incidents of election-related violence had been reported since last month.
The highest number of allegations were against the PA, the Centre for Monitoring Election Violence said in a statement.
